headline: Recommended approval of $126,030,888 FY27 budget 9-0, with a contingent restoration of a CMS music teacher position.
summary: The meeting covered 14 educational assistant positions and other special education staffing requests, and the budget's tax rate impact. Members discussed music instruction at CMS, and the Finance Committee made no formal recommendation on the budget adjustments. The board adopted an amendment to restore a 0.17 FTE music teacher position at CMS, contingent on the Superintendent's determination, then recommended the amended budget 9-0.
decisions: Approved an amendment to reduce the Superintendent Contingency and restore the 0.17 FTE music teacher position at CMS, contingent on the Superintendent's determination; motion passed with no individual roll call recorded.
Recommended approval of the 2026-2027 budget totaling $126,030,888, as amended, by a 9-0 vote.

plain_text:
Special Board Meeting – October 26, 2026 
Public Hearing and Vote on FY27 
 
In Attendance: Pamela Walsh – President, Cara Meeker – Vice President, Liz Boucher – Secretary, Jess 
Campbell, Alex Dubois, Brenda Hastings, Barb Higgins, Madeleine Mineau, and Sarah Sadowski 
 
Administration: Timothy Herbert – Superintendent, Jack Dunn, Kris Gallo 
 
Call to Order 
Ms. Walsh called the meeting to order at 6:00PM and asked Ms. Boucher to take roll call attendance. 
 
It was stated that the purpose of this meeting is to discuss finalization of the FY 2026-2027 budget. It 
was noted that any action taken during the meeting would require seven affirmative votes. 
 
Budget Presentation 
Administration presented updates following Finance Committee discussion. The committee did not 
make a formal recommendation on the proposed budget adjustments.
Board of Education Special Meeting – Public Hearing and Vote FY27 – October 26, 2026 Page 2 
 
Exclusive of Fund Balance in the amount of $1,700,000 (MAR 2026) and $1,707,302 (OCT 2026) 
 
Budget Adjustments Reviewed 
The presentation included: 
• Funding for 14 additional Educational Assistants (EAs). 
• Reallocation of funds to support special education staffing needs. 
• Memorial Field expenditures funded through trust funds. 
• Bleacher replacement funded through trust funds. 
• Adjustments to local and state revenue projections. 
• Updated expenditure and revenue estimates. 
Special Education Staffing Requests 
Administration requested consideration of: 
• Addition of 0.2 FTE Occupational Therapist at Broken Ground School. 
• Addition of 1.0 FTE Charter School Special Educator to provide required services to students 
attending charter and private schools. 
• Funding for 14 Educational Assistants to meet identified student needs. 
Administration explained that originally 23 Educational Assistant positions had been identified. 
Through staff reallocation and budget transfers, the need for additional funding was reduced to 14 
positions. 
 
Educational Assistant Distribution 
Identified staffing needs included: 
• Millbrook School: 9 positions
Board of Education Special Meeting – Public Hearing and Vote FY27 – October 26, 2026 Page 3 
• Abbott-Downing School: 4 positions 
• Broken Ground School: 5 positions 
• Concord Middle School: 2 positions 
• Rundlett Middle School: 1 position 
• Concord High School: 1 position 
• Additional support related to a foster placement outside the district 
Budget Reallocations 
Administration reported that savings were identified through: 
• Unfilled positions 
• Reduced transportation costs 
• Reduced contracted services 
• Students aging out of services 
• Vacant positions and resignations 
• Subscription and program savings 
These reallocations reduced the projected additional cost for special education staffing from 
approximately $860,876 to $477,876 for the remainder of the fiscal year. 
 
Future Staffing Concerns 
Board members asked what would occur if additional special education needs arise later in the school 
year. 
 
In response to questions about how the district would address the needs of additional special 
education students who may require services later in the year, administration explained that any 
unforeseen increases would likely necessitate mid-year budget reductions in other areas. This 
approach would be required to ensure continued compliance with students' Individualized Education 
Programs (IEPs) and the district’s legal obligation to provide appropriate services. 
 
Tax Rate and Revenue Discussion 
Administration reviewed the impact of valuation changes and budget adjustments on the tax rate. 
Highlights included: 
• Local education tax rate projected to decrease from $14.81 to $11.01 per $1,000 valuation. 
• Combined education tax rate projected to decrease from $16.39 to $12.10 per $1,000 
valuation. 
• The district's valuation increased significantly following reassessment.
Board of Education Special Meeting – Public Hearing and Vote FY27 – October 26, 2026 Page 4 
Administration explained that although the additional special education request totals approximately 
$477,876, the increase in local revenue exceeds $1 million because it also incorporates several other 
budget adjustments. These include workers’ compensation adjustments, appropriations for Memorial 
Field, and other budget changes that had been previously discussed during the budget development 
process. 
 
In response to questions about the addition of a Superintendent Contingency line, administration 
explained that a tax-rate "penny differential" generated approximately $62,000 in available funds. 
Rather than allowing those funds to be absorbed elsewhere in the budget, the recommendation was 
to place them in a Superintendent Contingency account to provide flexibility for unforeseen needs. 
 
Public Testimony 
Jessie Morency, speaking as both a special education advocate and parent, expressed concern that 
ongoing discussions about special education costs can unintentionally portray students as a financial 
burden. She thanked the Board for its commitment to supporting students and encouraged continued 
emphasis on the value and importance of all learners.  
 
Board members responded by reaffirming the district’s legal and moral responsibility to provide 
appropriate services and support for every student. 
 
Detailed Budget Review 
Administration reviewed line-by-line revenue and expenditure adjustments, including: 
Revenue Adjustments 
• Increased investment income earnings 
• Reduced rental revenue projections 
• Addition of Pittsfield contract revenue 
• Reduction in state adequacy aid 
• Additional unrestricted state aid 
• Increased catastrophic aid reimbursement 
• Preschool revenue adjustments 
• Tuition revenue updates 
• Net metering revenue projections 
• Trust fund transfers for Memorial Field and bleacher projects 
Expenditure Adjustments 
• Vocational reserve transfers 
• Pittsfield staffing expenditures 
• Workers’ compensation funding correction
Board of Education Special Meeting – Public Hearing and Vote FY27 – October 26, 2026 Page 5 
• Memorial Field expenditures 
• Bleacher replacement expenditures 
• Facility contingency increase related to mold remediation at Beaver Meadow School 
• Energy reserve transfers 
• Superintendent contingency funding 
• Raptor visitor management software 
Facility Contingency Discussion 
Administration explained that the facility contingency was increased by $100,000 to address mold 
remediation work at Beaver Meadow School. The issue stemmed from building settings that were not 
properly reset following weather-related adjustments. 
 
The Board also discussed elementary music staffing at CMS, with members expressing concern about 
the impact of staffing reductions on student access to music instruction. Questions centered on 
whether CMS students are receiving fewer music lessons than students at other elementary schools, 
whether staffing changes have created inequities among schools, and whether a previously reduced 
0.17 FTE music position should be restored. Administration acknowledged that music instruction 
frequency at CMS has decreased and that lesson schedules differ from prior years. It was further 
noted that staffing reductions have affected programs across the district and that restoring the 0.17 
FTE position would cost approximately $19,700. 
 
Moved by: Ms. Campbell 
Seconded by: Ms. Meeker
Board of Education Special Meeting – Public Hearing and Vote FY27 – October 26, 2026 Page 6 
Amendment Motion 
Motion 
To reduce the Superintendent Contingency and restore the 0.17 FTE music teacher position at CMS, 
contingent upon the Superintendent determining that: 
1. CMS students are receiving fewer music lessons than students at other elementary schools; or 
2. CMS music class sizes are significantly larger than those in other schools. 
Moved by: Ms. Walsh 
Seconded by: Ms. Sadowski 
Vote on Amendment 
Result: Motion Passed 
(No individual roll call was recorded for the amendment.) 
 
Final Vote on Budget as amended 
Roll Call Vote 
Board Member Vote 
Ms. Campbell Yes 
Mr. Dubois Yes 
Ms. Hastings Yes 
Ms. Higgins Yes 
Ms. Meeker Yes 
Ms. Mineau Yes 
Ms. Sadowski Yes 
Ms. Walsh Yes 
Ms. Boucher Yes 
Result 
Motion Passed, 9-0. 
 
Additional Discussion 
A Board member suggested that school districts consider invoicing the state to illustrate the financial 
impact of state underfunding of public education. Discussion acknowledged ongoing concerns 
regarding adequacy funding and court rulings related to state education funding obligations. 
 
Nonpublic Session 
Motion 
To enter nonpublic session under RSA 91-A:3 for discussion of personnel matters and a potential 
contract. 
Moved by: Ms. Walsh 
Seconded by: Ms. Boucher 
Adjournment 
Approved by roll call vote.
Board of Education Special Meeting – Public Hearing and Vote FY27 – October 26, 2026 Page 7 
The Board entered nonpublic session. It was noted that following the nonpublic session the Board 
would return solely for adjournment. (Moved by Ms. Walsh, 2nd by Ms. Boucher). 
 
Meeting adjourned into Non-Public at 6:55PM. 
 
Respectfully submitted, Sarah LeMay
